Same baseline, so the whole milestone is reviewed at the new SHA. Acceptance criteria: SCHED_TOKEN_ACL_1_PLAN.md with its 'Amendment 2026-10-11' (S1', S2' supersede S1, S2). Windows ACL behaviour is Windows-qualified; the Windows re-run on the final commit is owner-side. Integration none.
review_focus: check-and-refuse design (plan Amendment 2026-10-11): a new state folder is created locked by CreateDirectoryW with O:<sid>D:P(A;OICI;FA;;;<sid>); an existing folder is only checked through one handle opened with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT (owner, protected single-entry DACL, not a link) and every item inside must be a non-link owned by the user with no explicit entry for another SID; otherwise run exits 4 without changing anything
secure-state: refuses while the scheduler runs or when a link is inside, keeps the old folder renamed aside, copies plain files into a new locked folder, and the result passes the check

the token: created empty in the checked folder, own non-inherited user-only entry (POSIX 0600) before it is written; fail-closed exit 4 with no token left; no regression in the scheduler service, bearer-token check, service.json or the Living UI client reading api-token

ctypes correctness of security_of / _create_locked_folder (argtypes, handle and LocalFree handling, SDDL parsing) since Windows cannot be run in the review; the tests prove S1'-S4 on POSIX and do not pass vacuously, Windows tests are explicitly Windows-qualified
deployment impact recorded in the plan: existing installs and scheduler_task_ctl.ps1 -Action install need one secure-state run; is anything else that starts the service broken
